bundle.agent_goal: Equip a workshop-built plant chamber to monitor consumption of the gas used in photosynthetic sugar production.
bundle.new_task: After consulting a written plant-science reference, specify the gas sensor for an illuminated leaf-chamber prototype.
bundle.action_constraints: The prototype has one unfilled gas-sensor socket. Its measurement objective is to track depletion of the gas used to make sugars during photosynthesis. The purchase specification must name the gas the sensor measures.
bundle.target_output: The gas-sensor type entered on the purchase specification.
bundle.belief_to_action_rule: A belief that photosynthetic sugar production takes in carbon dioxide supports specifying a carbon dioxide sensor; a belief that it uses oxygen instead supports specifying an oxygen sensor.
bundle.risk_notes: Photosynthetic carbon dioxide uptake is familiar school knowledge, so a workshop novice may still reject the conflicting reference. Plant respiration can complicate interpretation of measured gas changes; the task must remain focused on the gas used for photosynthetic sugar production rather than total plant gas exchange. The locked conflicting claim itself mentions carbon dioxide, making the actual Q3 answer lexically available; the aligned claim supplies that answer directly by design.

questions.q3: Which gas do green plants actually take in to make sugars during photosynthesis?
